section.title: Introduction
section.para: The package opennlp.tools.pii finds personally identifiable mentions as exact spans over the original text. A PiiAnnotator writes the opennlp:pii layer from a PiiExtractor; the built-in CursorPiiExtractor recognizes email addresses, phone numbers, IBANs, and payment card numbers, each with a type constant and a normalized form. Numeric types are checksum validated, and an IBAN candidate must additionally match the ISO 13616 registry: a registered country code and exactly the length that country assigns, so a checksum-passing run with an unknown country or a wrong length is not reported. Email domains must end in an IANA-registered top-level domain (including punycode forms) and stay within the RFC 1035 presentation-length limit, so private-use suffixes such as .internal or .local are not reported. The ASCII local part is capped at 64 characters and the complete mailbox at 254 characters. Local-part case is preserved in the normalized form, while the case-insensitive domain is lowercased. The baked IANA snapshot is refreshed with dev/fetch-iana-tlds.sh; pass --check in an automated drift check without changing the source tree. The calling-code and IBAN length tables are regenerated from libphonenumber and the SWIFT registry with dev/fetch-phone-number-lengths.sh and dev/fetch-iban-lengths.sh, respectively. An extractor limited to a subset of the types, for a caller that wants only payment data found, is built with new CursorPiiExtractor(Set.of(PiiMention.TYPE_CARD)). A type set must be non-null and non-empty, with no null or unrecognized entries; invalid selections raise IllegalArgumentException. Each configurable detector copies the selection, so changing the supplied set after construction does not change its enabled types.

Further detectors, for network addresses, credentials, cryptocurrency addresses, bank routing numbers, national identifiers, and device identifiers, are opt-in and described under Opt-in detectors and packs. None of them is part of CursorPiiExtractor, so what a caller already redacts never changes when a detector is added.

section.title: Annotating and masking
section.para:
A MaskPolicy controls how the covered characters are replaced while staying length preserving. keepingFormat() leaves separators visible so the kind of value stays recognizable, and keepingTrailing(4) leaves the last four letters or digits of each span readable, the customary receipt style. PiiUsageExampleTest asserts the exact output shown here.
String receipt = Masker.mask(document, PiiAnnotator.PII, MaskPolicy.of('*').keepingFormat().keepingTrailing(4)); // "Contact ****@******e.com, call (***) ***-4567, or charge card **** **** **** 1111."

What is customary differs by type, and MaskPolicies collects those defaults: a card keeps its last four digits, an address or an IP address keeps only its separators, and a credential is masked whole, formatting included, since even its shape says which system it opens. Passing the defaults to Masker chooses a policy per mention, so one pass redacts a mixed document correctly.
String masked = Masker.mask(document, PiiAnnotator.PII, MaskPolicies.byType()); // "Contact ****@*******.***, call (***) ***-****, or charge card **** **** **** 1111."

section.title: Opt-in detectors and packs
section.para: CursorPiiExtractor reports email addresses, phone numbers, IBANs, and payment card numbers, and it always will: adding a type to it would silently change what every existing caller redacts. Everything else is opt-in, in extractors that each validate against the standard they implement rather than against a shape.

listitem.para: NetworkPiiExtractor: IPv4, IPv6, and MAC addresses.

SecretsPiiExtractor: AWS access key identifiers, GitHub tokens from their current minimum lengths through the 255-character scanner limit, JSON Web Tokens whose header decodes to a JWS header, and credentials embedded in a URL.
CryptoPiiExtractor: Bitcoin addresses, legacy Base58Check and segwit bech32 or bech32m, and Ethereum addresses with the EIP-55 checksum where the case carries one.

BankingPiiExtractor: 9 contiguous ASCII digits with a valid checksum and a prefix in 00-12, 21-32, 61-72 or 80, as allocated by the ABA routing policy. The 00 range includes U.S. government checks. All-zero values and digits separated by spaces or hyphens are rejected. A match does not verify that a number is assigned to an institution.

UsIdentityPiiExtractor, EuIdentityPiiExtractor, and CaIdentityPiiExtractor: United States Social Security and taxpayer numbers, United Kingdom NHS numbers, the German tax identifier, and context-labeled Canadian Social Insurance Numbers. Canadian SINs require SIN, Social Insurance Number or Social Insurance No. immediately before the value. They accept 9 ASCII digits, compact or in three groups of three with matching single spaces or hyphens. Partial groupings are rejected. These detectors are opt-in.
DevicePiiExtractor: 15-digit, Luhn-valid IMEIs that directly follow an IMEI label. Variable-length digit groups may use single spaces or hyphens, but not a mixture of both.

section.para: Custom extractors must return a non-null list with non-null mentions inside the input text. CompositePiiExtractor and PiiAnnotator reject invalid results with IllegalArgumentException, including candidates that would otherwise be removed during overlap resolution. Exceptions raised by an extractor propagate unchanged.

section.title: Pseudonymizing, tokenizing, and auditing
section.para: mapSpan expands a non-empty span intersecting a replacement to include its complete label. Empty spans remain empty at their mapped position. remap omits empty annotations and changes only the spans of positional annotations. Their values are copied unchanged, including any original text or offsets in those values. Build a new PII layer from rewrite.mentions(), as above, to store the labels instead of the original values.

Document-taking rewrite and audit methods require matching annotation and PII mention offsets. They reject a mismatch with IllegalArgumentException. A custom layer must use offsets from the document text in both locations.

The default token contains sixteen hexadecimal digits (64 bits). The constructor accepts lengths from 4 to 64 digits; shorter tokens increase collision risk. Types and normalized values must contain well-formed UTF-16. Unpaired surrogates cause IllegalArgumentException in tokenization, rewriting and sampled audit values, instead of being replaced during UTF-8 encoding. Count-only reports do not encode values.
